To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
two DHA derived fatty-acid amides, N docosapentaenoyl dopamine and docosahexeoyl serotonin are more potent mediates of inflammatory processes than DHA.

two DHA derived fatty acids amides, N docosohexaenoyldopamine (DHDA) as well as docosahexanoyl serotonin (5 HT) are more potent mediatory of inflammatory responses than DHA and that the endocannabionoid tone is altered by a combination of ER as well as n 3 PUA in a human intervention study.

two novel fatty acid amide conjugates of DHA exert potent anti-inflammatory effects in vitro, that the postprandrial EC tone is altered in response to a combination of energy restriction and n3 PUFA intake and that the endocannabionoid system plays an important role during obesity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of new endogenous mediators of inflammation and their potential roles in obesity and metabolic disease.
the role of endocannabinoids in the pathogenesis and treatment of inflammatory and metabolic disorders.

the identification of new endogenous lipid mediators with potential anti-inflammatory properties, and the exploration of the effects of a diet enriched in n 3 PUA on endocannabinoids in relation to obesity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DHA derived fatty acids amides, such as DHA 5HT and DHDA have potent anti-inflammatory activities, and may be considered as novel therapeutic targets for inflammatory diseases.
our findings provide new insights into the role of DHA derived FA as mediators of inflammatory and metabolic processes.
DHA is an important precursor in the synthesis of DHA derived FAAS which are more potent than DHA itself in suppressing inflammatory processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the endocannibinoid system is an important regulator of inflammatory processes and that n 3 Pufas, and their metabolites may play a role in this process.

the formation of DHEA and other endocannabinoids derived fatty acid amide metabolites of n 3 PUFAs may be a novel mechanism underlying the beneficial health effects and anti-inflammatory properties of omega 3 fatty acid rich diets and that the ECS is involved in the regulation of food intake.

DHA derived fatty acids amides are more potent than the parent compound DHA and that a combination of energy restriction and n 3 fatty acids can alter endocannabinoid levels in plasma, which may be involved in the beneficial effects of n 4 PUFAs on metabolic health.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the endocannbinoid system is not a single target for the treatment of obesity but a network of targets that are all involved in the pathophysiology of obesity and its comorbidities.

DHA derived fatty amide conjugates, which are formed by enzymatic action in the body, are potent modulators of inflammatory processes and may thus contribute to the beneficial health effects associated with the consumption of DHA.
the fatty acid composition of the diet can modulate the ECS and that this may contribute to the beneficial effects of n  3 PUFA rich diets on metabolic health.
